definition: Pain mechanisms are the underlying processes by which pain is produced and experienced. In this source, they are presented as an important but often insufficiently covered topic in antenatal education, where better understanding of how pain works may support coping, confidence, and pain management during labour and after birth.

reasons: The opening definition of pain mechanisms as “the underlying processes by which pain is produced and experienced” is not stated or clearly defined in the source packet.

The packet supports that pain mechanisms are under-addressed in antenatal education and that pain-focused education may help with labour and postpartum pain, but it does not support the broader explanatory definition given in the first sentence.

The packet does not define or describe what “pain mechanisms” are (the definition’s first sentence claims they are “underlying processes by which pain is produced and experienced,” which is not supported by the provided text).

The packet supports that “pain mechanisms and postpartum pain remain under-addressed” and that pain neuroscience principles may enhance antenatal education and support more effective pain management, but it does not specifically state that “better understanding of how pain works” may directly support coping and confidence during labour/after birth.
